newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's BCH results encouraging - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Spain's BCH results encouraging - analysts.

text.p: Spain's Banco Central Hispano's (BCH) nine-month results confirm the bank is over the worst and beginning to reap the benefits of its recent rationalisation, analysts said on Friday.
"They were good results, but the fact that profits (before minorities) reached 33 billion pesetas had already been discounted by the market," an analyst said.
The bank posted a 20 percent increase in attributable profits on Thursday to 27.31 billion pesetas for the nine months to September 1996.
BCH said the results reflected an improvement in retail and corporate banking business, as well as the benefits from its cost and structural rationalisation.
But some analysts pointed out that the bank had failed to increase its net provisions, which fell 42.4 percent to 31.854 billion pesetas.
"I think it should be more aggressive in providing for bad debts," said one analyst.

The bank's debt coverage ratio without mortgages rose to 86.5 percent from 85 percent in the same period in 1995, and non-performing loans accounted for 4.1 percent of total loans compared with 5.4 percent in 1995.
Analysts said they expected profits to improve next year thanks to the expansion of business in Latin America.

The bank has said it is pursuing an international expansion strategy focussing on Latin America, and added Banco de Colombia to its interests on Thursday as it said it plans to buy 26 to 36 percent of its capital.
Analysts also said they were encouraged by the stabilisation of the bank's dividend after it paid only one dividend (75 pesetas) last year due to restructuring.
The bank's board said on Thursday it would pay an interim dividend of 50 pesetas a share gross and a final dividend of 50 pesetas or more.
